messages:
incident-bot: Paging eng-oncall: p99 latency spike detected for /v1/streaming/generate in us-west-2. Metric: p99 > 2.5s for the last 5m (SLO 500ms). Error rate stable. Paging level: P1.
pagerduty-bot: @Aisha you are the primary oncall. Escalation to Tom if not ack in 5m.
Aisha: acked. jumping in. seeing p95 rising too. rolling dashboard now. any customer alerts?
Maya: support: 4 tickets flagged slow responses, one customer noted stalled streaming frames (kept reconnecting). no batch job changes in last 30m per deploy-bot.
Aisha: ok - priority: 1) confirm scope (hosted/dedicated/private) 2) isolate path (streaming vs sync) 3) quick mitigation if customer impact.
Sven: looks isolated to streaming endpoints hitting the continuous-batching path on the serving runtime. I see queue length spike on batcher nodes -> a few oversized batches stuck at tail.
Tom: interesting. any sign of mixed sequence length amplification? i.e., long sequences pulling smaller ones into same kernel and blocking preempt?
Sven: yeah. seqlen distribution shifted — a handful of very long sequences (>= 8k tokens) interleaved with lots of short ones. continuous-batcher default max_batch_tokens set to 4096; scheduler fairness is tilting toward max fill -> big batches.
Aisha: paste the metrics and logs pls.
Sven: pulling logs. snippet: ```
[2025-11-03T14:12:07Z] batcher: created batch id=abcd size_tokens=11872 items=5 seq_lens=[102,128,96,8196,125]
[2025-11-03T14:12:07Z] kernel: started batch abcd
[2025-11-03T14:12:09Z] kernel: batch abcd preempt_attempt=0 waited_ms=1800
[2025-11-03T14:12:09Z] batcher: tail_latency=2.2s
```
Tom: that shows a single long sequence inflating batch token count. kernel expected preemption but didn't because preempt config was off for streaming path.
Aisha: is this a config drift or new traffic pattern?
Sven: traffic shift. a new internal customer started a very long summarization job around 14:00 which aligns.
Kevin: tagging product: happened after #internal-batch-run kicked off. cc @Maya for customers.
Maya: telling customers it's being investigated. no SLA incidents yet but could hit sustained p99 if not mitigated.
Aisha: proposed quick mitigations (in order): 1) enable preemptive-shedding for continuous-batcher (allow kernel preemption on streaming path) 2) lower max_batch_tokens for streaming to 2048 3) route streaming traffic to streaming-only pool (smaller batch target) 4) temporarily block super-long sequences via rate limit/short-circuit. Which is fastest?
Tom: fastest is config flip: lower max_batch_tokens + enable preempt. that can be applied via rollout to config map on batcher fleet; low blast radius. routing change needs a routing-table push and may be slower.
Sven: I can push a targeted config to the us-west-2 batcher pool. will keep default for other regions.
Aisha: do it. runbook step id: RB-serve-008. leave rollback steps.
Sven: executing: ```kubectl apply -f /ops/batcher-configs/streaming-preempt-usw2.yaml```
ops-bot: deploy-batcher-config job started by Sven (job=cfg-7554).
Sven: change applied. enabling preemptive_shedding=true and max_batch_tokens=2048 on service=batcher-usw2-streaming.
Tom: monitoring. watch p99 and tail latency panels. also trace a stuck request id if one appears.
Aisha: Maya, tell support we expect improvement in 2-3 min post-change. keep customers updated.
Maya: message sent to affected customers; added temporary note to status page.
Sven: preliminary metrics: 60s after change p99 dropped from 2.6s -> 520ms, p95 back to ~200ms. queue length down 45%.
Tom: nice. any error bump from preemption?
Sven: small number of aborted streaming frames (0.03% increase) while long sequences got short-circuited. acceptable trade.
Aisha: ok, hold mitigation for 10m, if stable promote to canary across us-west-2 pools and then to global. open follow-up ticket to add automatic detection of oversized seqs and adaptive batch caps.
Kevin: filing ticket INF-1429: "adaptive-seqlen-protection for continuous-batcher" with suggested owner: Sven, priority P2.
pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by oncall. Timeline note created.
Tom: handoff: I can take next shift on this if it persists. Aisha -> handing to Tom at 14:24Z.
Aisha: handoff noted. thanks team.
Maya: monitoring customer replies. customers are seeing faster responses now. one customer had to restart client but no data loss.
Sven: rolling global rollout now (canary 10% -> 50%). will watch for regressions: memory pressure, kernel retries.
Sven: small regression in kernel retry metric in eu-west-1 when canary set to 50% (some models with long KV caches push memory > threshold). rolling back eu-west-1 canary, leaving us-west-2 canonical.
Tom: note for postmortem: - add guardrail to avoid >max_tokens per batch when mixed seqlen present - consider preemption default for streaming - surface long-seq spikes in routing console
Aisha: agreed. closing live mitigation if metrics stable for 30m and customer reports clear. leaving incident open for postmortem and follow-ups (INF-1429).
Maya: closing customer comms after final confirmation.
incident-bot: Incident P1 -> status: mitigated (live mitigation applied). Assigning postmortem owner: Sven.
